correctness.rationale: For n iid uniform circle points, cyclic gaps equal independent Exp(1) variables divided by their sum. In the critical m=log_2(n)+O(1) window, union bounds ensure the m+1 gaps inspected from any vertex span less than a semicircle with probability 1-o(1), so missing clockwise/counterclockwise candidate flags are the exponential inequalities A_i={Z_{i-1}>sum_{r=0}^{m-1} Z_{i+r}} and B_i={Z_i>sum_{r=1}^m Z_{i-r}}. Each has exact probability 2^-m. Same-direction locally overlapping events at cyclic offset 1<=k<=m have joint probability 4^-m(2/3)^k; same-gap reverse events and other opposite orientations are bounded by (4/9)^m after conditioning and exponential Laplace transforms; support disjointness gives dependency graph degree O(m). Consequently Chen–Stein local dependence bounds TV from Poisson(2n2^-m) by O(n m (4/9)^m), which tends to zero in the stated critical window. In the supercritical-coverage regime use a union bound for m<=O(log n), and monotonicity with a capped logarithmic m for larger m; below threshold a pair-covariance variance estimate and Chebyshev give P(no missing flags)->0. When every directional edge is present, greedy descent on the nearest-neighbor bidirectional cycle reaches a nearest stored point for every query and every start; with a missing side, a query immediately beyond the midpoint of that adjacent gap makes a nonoptimal blocked local minimum. Numerical Monte Carlo (400000 independent exponential windows at six pairs m<=3) agrees with the exact same-orientation pair formula within roughly three sampling SD and the source checker is finite. Boundary caveat: the source text additionally claims all-m exact coupling outside the sole event of an individual gap>=1/2. This is stronger than needed and may fail for very large m if an m-gap arc spans a semicircle. The actual theorem follows using the explicitly supplied capped-m monotonicity argument, without relying on an all-m exact coupling. No finite-n all-m identity is accepted as part of the proved final finding.
